standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation are fpqc local on the base
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-descending-property-finite, lemma-descending-property-flat and lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-presentation, invoked at proof lines 6454-6457

core_obligations: Reduce 'finite locally free' to finite, flat and locally of finite presentation and apply the three descending lemmas (proof lines 6451-6457).
For the degree version, note that for finite locally free f the degree at a point u is read off from (f_* O_Z)_u tensor kappa(u) (proof lines 6458-6462).
Conclude that a surjective family of base changes all of degree d forces the original morphism to have degree d, hence fpqc locality of the degree-d property (proof lines 6458-6462).
proof_roadmap: First assertion by decomposition and three descending lemmas (proof lines 6451-6457).
Degree read off from the fibre of the pushforward, giving the second assertion (proof lines 6458-6462).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts fpqc locality on the base both for 'finite locally free' and, for each d >= 0, for 'finite locally free of degree d' (statement lines 6441-6448). For the first, the proof decomposes the property into finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation by the equivalence with finite flat locally finitely presented morphisms, and quotes the three corresponding descending lemmas. For the second it gives a displayed reason rather than a citation: if a finite locally free f becomes of degree d after a surjective family of base changes, then d can be read off at a point u from the fibre (f_* O_Z)_u tensor kappa(u), which is computed after base change and is therefore d everywhere (proof lines 6450-6462). The level is H2: one part is an assembly of three already-established descent statements and the other is a short displayed computation of the degree.
